newsitem.title: CHINA: 14 dead, 3 missing in south China floods - paper.
newsitem.headline: 14 dead, 3 missing in south China floods - paper.

text.p: Heavy downpours caused severe flooding in the south China coastal province of Guangdong where 14 people have died and three are missing, a Hong Kong Chinese-language daily said on Sunday.
In the city of Maoming, the most affected region, 11 villagers were swept into a river as a bridge collapsed. Five people were drowned, the China-backed Ta Kung Pao said.
The report did not give further details.
Weather authorities in the provincial capital Guangzhou said the rainfall recorded this year was the highest for several decades.
The province had been hit by heavy rains since last week, but rainfall had been continuous and the capital city Guangzhou had seen only four dry days since the beginning of June, the report said.
Floods had caused the province economic losses estimated at over 300 million yuan (US$39 million), the paper said.
In central Guangdong's Qingxin city, heavy rainfall flooded farmland, trapped thousands of people and suspended the electricity supply, the report said.
Major roads in the eastern city of Jieyang were blocked, posing difficulties to the rescue work in the area.
According to the provincial government, the level of the Bei Jiang river, a tributary of the Yangtze river, exceeded warning levels on Friday.
The provincial government had already stepped up flood control measures and typhoon checks, the report said.
